figures.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: original explanatory figure for a Korean research-project README, landscape
Primary request: a crisp publication-quality concept illustration of offline dashcam review, arranged as three balanced panels on a white background.
Panel A: stylized realistic daylight front dashcam view of a three-lane road, rear of two anonymous cars visible; one car partially crosses a dashed lane boundary. No license plate characters or identifiable locations.
Panel B: one rear-vehicle crop and a short abstract sequence of amber lamp observations, with an occluded frame visibly gray rather than declared off. This is a concept, NOT a measured result.
Panel C: a person-free minimal review monitor showing a timeline, selected interval and two separate outputs representing annotated preview and original clip.
Style/medium: restrained academic illustration, accurate road perspective, navy lines, teal and amber accents, clean readable sans serif, generous margins, no ornamental branding.
Text (verbatim): heading "OFFLINE DASHCAM REVIEW"; panel labels "A  OBSERVATION", "B  TEMPORAL CONTEXT", "C  HUMAN REVIEW"; footer "CONCEPT ILLUSTRATION - NOT A DETECTION RESULT".
Constraints: English labels only, no accuracy percentages, no police, no accusation, no real footage or identifiable people, no logos, no watermark; no invented experimental charts. Wide 16:9 composition with readable labels at README width.
figures.scope: Explanatory concept, not footage, model output, UI implementation or evaluation evidence.

figures.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram
Asset type: original research-method overview figure, landscape, GitHub README
Primary request: a clean publication-quality two-row architecture infographic on white, with generous margins and large legible English typography. It must clearly distinguish implemented library APIs from unimplemented future event analysis.
Top row titled "IMPLEMENTED LIBRARY PATH": six simple illustrated boxes connected by solid navy arrows, labels exactly "Source PTS", "Detector interface", "Same-frame batch", "VFR tracker", "Coded review", "Preview + clip". Small supporting labels respectively "FFmpeg", "Caller supplied", "Original coordinates", "OpenCV", "Observation / prediction", "MP4 + time mapping". Detector interface means model injected by caller, not automatic bundled detection.
Bottom row titled "PLANNED EVENT ANALYSIS": four gray outlined boxes connected by dashed gray arrows, labels "Lane-change candidate", "Lamp ROI sequence", "Usable / unknown", "Human validation". A dashed branch descends from the VFR tracker box to the bottom row; no arrow claims those parts are implemented.
Footer text exactly "Local processing | Exact source time | Not a violation decision".
Style: minimalist academic method diagram, navy for implemented path, amber for uncertain observation icon, gray for planned work; a few tasteful road/camera/batch/timeline/review/file miniature illustrations; no decorative gradients.
Constraints: no accuracy metrics, no actual vehicle detections, no logos, no watermark, no dense unreadable text, no fake paper citation. Wide 16:9 image. Both row titles and all six top labels / four bottom labels must be correct and readable.
figures.scope: Solid path: implemented library APIs. Dashed path: planned event analysis. Icons and times are illustrative.
Actual rendered image from deterministic pattern video and scripted post-NMS boxes; NOT model detections or driving accuracy.
Actual native predicted position with no current vehicle observation; age 1/10 second. Scripted synthetic input, not detector accuracy.
Actual render of two identical class-2 detections and a separate class-5 observation; ambiguous raw boxes carry no identity. Not a real vehicle event.

diagrams.scope: Directly authored vector diagram of implemented source/PTS verification, recorded-input replay and atomic output. Not footage, detection output, performance evidence or a GUI.

notes: Original explanatory assets; no third-party paper figures copied.
Generated concepts are not scientific evidence. Captions distinguish synthetic experiments, implemented APIs and planned algorithms.
